description: An engineering manager must approve a four-week pager rotation for a newly supported API, including primary and secondary coverage, customer escalation ownership, and security escalation coverage, after the normal cross-functional roster review.

shared_context.S1: The new payments API enters 24-hour production support next Monday.
shared_context.S2: Morgan makes the final decision on the four-week pager roster.
shared_context.S3: The draft roster assigns Maya and Leo as alternating backend primaries, Jordan and Rina as alternating SRE secondaries, and leaves daytime customer escalation and security escalation unspecified.
shared_context.S4: The support policy requires one primary and one secondary for every week, with no person serving in both roles during the same week.
shared_context.S5: Before publishing a production pager roster, Morgan conducts a round-robin review with backend engineering, SRE, customer support, and security engineering.

PF1.text: While arranging an unrelated team handoff this morning, Priya confirmed that Maya is unavailable during week 3 and that Leo is the only current backend engineer trained to troubleshoot the payments webhook path; she has not updated the draft roster yet.

PF2.text: While reconciling the database rotation this afternoon, Jon found that Jordan is already assigned as the database primary during week 2 and cannot also be the payments API secondary that week; Rina is available to cover it, but Jon has not recorded the collision in the roster document.

PF3.text: During a customer account review today, Elena confirmed that Acme Health's support agreement requires a named support escalation owner who can respond within 15 minutes on weekdays from 08:00 to 18:00 UTC, and Dana is the only support specialist currently trained for that account; the contract note is still in the support system.

PF4.text: While completing a token-classification review this morning, Kai confirmed that the payments API must have Kai assigned as its security escalation contact for weeks 1 and 2, followed by an access review exactly 30 days after the roster is published; the security finding has not yet been attached to the roster ticket.

acceptance_conditions: Leo must be the payments API primary during week 3.
Rina must be the payments API secondary during week 2.
Dana must be the named customer escalation owner.
Kai must be the security escalation contact for both weeks 1 and 2.
The security access review must be scheduled exactly 30 days after publication.
The settlement must cite the backend availability and webhook-training constraint.
The settlement must cite the database-rotation collision.
The settlement must cite the Acme Health response requirement.
The settlement must cite the security escalation and access-review requirement.

decisive_facts.why: Maya's week-3 unavailability changes the week-3 primary from the draft rotation to Leo, while Leo's webhook training makes Leo the required trained backend coverage for that week.
Jordan's existing database-primary assignment changes the week-2 secondary from Jordan to the available Rina.
Acme Health's 15-minute weekday requirement changes the unspecified customer escalation owner to the specifically trained Dana.
The token-classification requirement changes unspecified security escalation to Kai for weeks 1 and 2 and sets the access review to exactly 30 days after publication.
